title: ComfyUI
subtitle: A node-based media pipeline runs as a GPU media studio behind my memory gateway, with provenance tracked on every generated asset.

stats.label: media tools any agent can call
frames in the video workflows that render and deliver end to end

lede: FAFOHive hosts a GPU media studio as tools any agent can call, and ComfyUI is its render engine. The risk I saw was agents treating a GPU and a third-party HTTP engine as free and repeatable: a retried render costs GPU time, a crash mid-render leaves an unknown outcome, and an agent-supplied Docker or shell option is an escape hatch. I decided to leave ComfyUI unmodified and put all of the control in a Rust controller in front of it. ComfyUI's own APIs do the rendering; I built no engine and changed none of its code. A render's identity is written down before ComfyUI sees the request, so a crash never pays for the same render twice.
quote: When agents are the callers, I wrap third-party engines in idempotent, crash-safe control and place the human decision at the licence boundary.
evidence: Governed AI media pipelines: 33 media tools for agents on an unmodified ComfyUI engine behind a Rust controller that accepts typed choices only, with no Docker options, mounts or shell strings.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: render identity persisted before submission, uncertain outcomes reconciled against the engine and never resubmitted, outputs registered immutably.
Human approval at the licence boundary: model downloads approved by a person at a local console that no remote call can reach, then resumable, hash-checked and registered.
author: Corey James
